item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence supports separating training discrimination from retrieval quality. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found that negative-sampling choices change accuracy and head/mid/tail performance; aggregate scores hide these differences. Earlier [sampled-metric analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) establishes that sampled and full-catalog metrics can produce inconsistent model rankings. A [2024 reproduction study](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989/) further attributes substantial disagreement about popularity bias to evaluation strategy and user grouping. Consequently, loader-negative margins alone cannot establish actionable ranking improvement: easy sampled negatives may conceal competition from popular or otherwise highly scored catalog items.\n\nFor this task, the practical inference is to retain pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 as the sole selection criterion, while auditing fixed training-only prefixes against both sampled candidates and the full unseen catalog. Define diagnostic targets strictly within training histories, preserve temporal order, and exclude prefix-seen items. Report retrieval HR/rank, recommendation coverage, popularity concentration, and performance by training-derived item popularity and history length; do not infer unobserved simulator traits. Quantify paired model differences by resampling users within each category and recomputing the four-category macro mean, reporting category-specific intervals and subgroup counts. Separately vary diagnostic candidate seeds and uniform/popularity sampling to expose candidate sensitivity; these checks leave official evaluation unchanged. Treat this as an audit design, not an established predictor of validation gains: test whether diagnostic changes track actual validation improvements across trials. Budget diagnostics explicitly using capped users/prefixes, batched catalog scoring, sparse checkpoint frequency, and recorded GPU seconds; bootstrap cached per-user outcomes on CPU."}
